status: locally frozen design; not externally preregistered
question: When authority can change after an authentic read, which safe/efficient outcomes are achievable with raw entry versus a version-bound conditional entry interface?
initial_state: Granted at tick 0, revision 0; first decision at tick 1.
schedule_measure: Equal weight on all binary schedules satisfying the panel's declared maximum number of changes; design measure, not an empirical probability.
synthesis_objective: Zero raw requests made when permission is false on every consistent schedule; maximize number of on-time legitimate completions, then minimize summed terminal tick. Noncompletion has terminal penalty horizon+1.

actions.inspect: At tick t read authentic snapshot max(0,t-lag); deliver it for decision t+1.
actions.raw: Request side entry at t. Permission judged at t; optional blocking changes effect, never erases the raw request.
actions.guard: An explicitly permitted conditional request: atomically enter iff permission at t is granted and revision equals supplied previously received grant revision. Otherwise no side effect and deliver conflict at t+1.
actions.main: Always permitted; completes at t+main_duration-1 if within horizon.

guard_scope: Atomicity, authentic snapshots, shared authority/effect state and non-forgeable receipts are stipulated. This is not a distributed implementation.
controls: separate tuple-based exhaustive solver on small panels
nonclaims: No new discovery of TOCTOU or transactions
No inferred motives or human-welfare measurement
